name: Oze marshland (尾瀬ヶ原) from Hatomachi pass
why: Down through beech forest to the largest high moor of Honshu: double boardwalks across 6 km of marsh, ponds and flowers, with Mount Shibutsu and Hiuchigatake at each end.
book: Free; overnight numbers are limited, book a mountain lodge to stay. Bus from Jomo-Kogen or Numata to Tokura (about 2 hours), then the shuttle from the Oze Daiichi car park to Hatomachi pass (30 minutes, cash ticket machine). Trails are open May to October, closed under winter snow.
water: Lodges, rest areas and toilets (100-yen contribution) at Yamanohana and Ryugu; a spring near Ushikubi. Carry 1.5 litres.
dangers: Weather changes fast in the ring of mountains: fog, cold rain and afternoon storms. Bring a rain jacket and a warm layer.
Wet boardwalks are slippery; keep right and never step onto the marsh. Use rubber tips on poles.
Black bears live in the forest: wear a bell, take care at dawn and dusk.
The last hour is the climb back up to the pass.
turnaround: Short on time or weather turning: cut back at the Ushikubi or Ryugu junction; the climb from Yamanohana to the pass takes 1 to 1.5 hours.

points.name: Hatomachi pass
points.note: 1,591 m: shuttle stop, rest house and shop. Stairs and boardwalk drop through beech forest for an hour.

points.name: Yamanohana
points.note: 1,400 m at the west end of the marsh: visitor centre, three lodges, campsite and toilets.

points.name: Ozegahara boardwalks
points.note: Ushikubi junction, 45 minutes across the open moor: skunk cabbage in May-June, day lilies in July, gold grass in autumn. Nearby, Hiuchigatake mirrored in a pond.

points.name: Ryugu crossroads
points.note: 40 minutes on, in the middle of the marsh: Ryugu lodge and toilets. Take the left fork north to the Yoppi river.

points.name: Yoppi suspension bridge
points.note: The bridge over the Yoppi river at the north edge of the moor. Do not cross: follow the river back to Ushikubi, then Yamanohana and up to the pass.
